units.text: From heaven the Lord looked down; He saw all the sons of men.
From His prepared dwelling place He looked upon all who inhabit the earth.
He formed their hearts individually; He understands all their deeds.
The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

“And you, son of man, say to the ruler of Tyre: Thus says the Lord: Because your heart was exalted and you said, ‘I am a god; I have inhabited a god’s dwelling in the heart of the sea’—yet you are a human, and not a god, and you made your heart like a god’s heart—
Surely you are not wiser than Daniel? Did wise men not instruct you in their knowledge?
Surely it was not by your knowledge or understanding that you built up strength for yourself, and gold and silver in your treasuries?
By your abundant knowledge and your trade you increased your strength; your heart was exalted in your strength.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Since you made your heart like a god’s heart,

therefore, behold, I am bringing foreigners against you, scourges from nations. They will draw their swords against you and against the beauty of your knowledge, and lay your beauty out for destruction,
In the eleventh year, on the first of the month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,
“Son of man, because Tyre said of Jerusalem, ‘Well done! She is shattered; the nations have perished. She has turned to me; the full one has been laid waste,’
therefore thus says the Lord: I am against you, Tyre, and I will bring many nations against you, as the sea rises with its waves.
They will throw down Tyre’s walls and throw down your towers. I will winnow her dust from her and make her a smooth rock.
She will be a drying place for nets in the midst of the sea, for I have spoken, says the Lord. She will become plunder for the nations,
With his horses’ hoofs they will trample all your squares. He will kill your people with the sword and bring the support of your strength down to the ground.
He will plunder your strength, strip your possessions, throw down your walls, and demolish your desirable houses. He will throw your stones, timber, and dust into the sea.
He will put an end to the multitude of your musicians, and the sound of your psalteries will certainly no longer be heard.
I will make you a smooth rock, a drying place for nets. You will certainly not be rebuilt, for I have spoken, says the Lord.
Thus says the Lord: “For three impieties of Gaza, and for four, I will not turn away from them, because they took Solomon’s captives into captivity, to shut them up in Idumea.
I will send fire upon Gaza’s walls, and it will devour her foundations.
I will destroy inhabitants from Azotus, and a tribe will be removed from Ascalon. I will bring My hand against Accaron, and the remaining foreigners will perish,” says the Lord.
Thus says the Lord: “For three impieties of Tyre, and for four, I will not turn away from her, because they shut Solomon’s captives up in Idumea and did not remember a covenant of brothers.
I will send fire upon Tyre’s walls, and it will devour her foundations.”
For Gaza will be plundered and Ashkelon will disappear; Ashdod will be cast out at midday and Ekron uprooted.
Woe to the seacoast’s inhabitants, sojourners of Cretans! The Lord’s word is against you, Canaan, land of foreigners: I will destroy you from your dwelling.
Crete will become pasture for flocks and an enclosure for sheep,

and the seacoast will belong to the remnant of Judah’s house. They will graze upon them in Ashkelon’s houses; at evening they will lodge away from the sons of Judah, for the Lord their God has visited them and turned their captivity.
The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and the sons of Judah could not destroy them. The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem until that day.
When they drew near Jerusalem and came to Bethphage, to the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two disciples,
saying to them, “Go into the village opposite you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied up and a colt with her. Untie them and bring them to Me.
If anyone says anything to you, say, ‘The Lord has need of them,’ and immediately he will send them.”
This happened so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled:
“Tell the daughter of Zion: ‘Behold, your King comes to you, meek and mounted upon a donkey, and upon a colt, the foal of a beast of burden.’”
The disciples went and did as Jesus directed them.
They brought the donkey and the colt, placed the garments upon them, and He sat upon them.
Most of the crowd spread their garments on the road, while others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.
The crowds going before Him and those following cried out, “Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is the One coming in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!”
The next day, the great crowd that had come to the feast, hearing that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem,
took branches of the palm trees and went out to meet Him, and cried out, “Hosanna! Blessed is the One who comes in the name of the Lord, even the King of Israel!”
Jesus found a young donkey and sat upon it, just as it is written,
“Do not fear, daughter Zion. Behold, your King comes, sitting upon a donkey’s colt.”
His disciples did not understand these things at first. But when Jesus was glorified, then they remembered that these things were written about Him and that they had done these things to Him.
And he will descend like rain upon a fleece, and like drops dripping upon the earth.
Righteousness will arise in his days, and abundant peace until the moon is taken away.
And he will rule from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the inhabited world.
Ethiopians will fall before him, and his enemies will lick dust.
kings of Tarshish and the islands will offer gifts; kings of the Arabians and Saba will bring gifts.
And all kings will bow before him; all nations will serve him.
Moses took half the blood and poured it into bowls; the other half he poured against the altar.
He took the book of the covenant and read it in the hearing of the people. They said, “We will do and obey everything the Lord has spoken.”
Moses took the blood and sprinkled it over the people, saying, “Behold, the blood of the covenant the Lord has made with you concerning all these words.”
And when Joseph came to his brothers, they stripped Joseph of the tunic of many colours which was upon him.
And they took him and cast him into the pit; and the pit was empty, having no water.
But you will be called priests of the Lord, ministers of God. You will consume the nations’ resources and be admired in their wealth.
Thus they will inherit the land a second time, and everlasting joy will be over their head.
God will come from Teman, the Holy One from a mountain shaded and thickly wooded. Diapsalma. His excellence covered the heavens, and the earth is full of His praise.
His brightness will be like light; horns are in His hands, and He established mighty love of His strength.
A word will go before Him, and He will go out, His feet in sandals.
From the far-shining radiance before Him, the clouds passed— hail and coals of fire.
And the Lord thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave His voice.
And He sent out arrows and scattered them; He multiplied lightning flashes and threw them into turmoil.

For thus the Lord said to me: “As a lion or lion cub cries over prey it has caught and shouts over it until the mountains fill with its voice, and they are defeated and terrified by the greatness of its wrath, so the Lord Sabaoth will descend to march upon Mount Zion, upon her mountains.
Like flying birds, so the Lord will shield Jerusalem, rescue, preserve and save.”
For thus says the Lord: Behold, I will seek out My sheep and visit them.

As a shepherd seeks his flock on a day when there is gloom and cloud among separated sheep, so I will seek out My sheep and drive them away from every place where they scattered on a day of cloud and gloom.

I will bring them out from the nations, gather them from the countries and bring them into their own land. I will feed them upon Israel’s mountains, in the ravines and in every dwelling place of the land.
I will feed them in good pasture, and their folds will be upon Israel’s high mountain. There they will lie down, there rest in good delight, and graze in rich pasture upon Israel’s mountains.
I Myself will feed My sheep and give them rest, and they will know that I am the Lord. Thus says the Lord, the Lord:
I will seek the lost, bring back the wandering, bind up the broken, strengthen the failing and guard the strong. I will feed them with judgment.
Then the Lord became jealous for His land and spared His people.
The Lord answered His people: “Look, I am sending out to you grain, wine and oil, and you will be filled with them. I will no longer give you over to reproach among the nations,

Hast Thou utterly rejected Judah, and has Thy soul departed from Zion? Why didst Thou strike us, and there is no healing for us? We waited for peace, and there were no good things; for a time of healing, and behold, turmoil!
We recognized, Lord, our sins and our fathers’ injustices, because we sinned before Thee.
Abate for Thy name’s sake; do not destroy Thy throne of glory. Remember; do not shatter Thy covenant with us.
Is there among the nations’ idols one who brings rain? Can heaven give its fullness? Is it not Thou Thyself? And we will wait for Thee, because Thou madest all these things.
They see false things and divine vain things, those who say, ‘The Lord says,’ although the Lord has not sent them; and they began to establish a word.
Have you not seen a false vision and spoken vain divinations?
Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Because your words are false and your divinations vain, therefore behold, I am against you, says the Lord,

and I will stretch out My hand against the prophets who see false things and utter vain things. They will not belong to My people’s instruction, nor be written in the register of the house of Israel, nor enter Israel’s land. They will know that I am the Lord.
Because they misled My people, saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there was no peace, and this one builds a wall, and they coat it—if it is going to fall,
O shepherds who scatter and destroy the sheep of My pasture!
Therefore thus says the Lord to those shepherding My people: You scattered My sheep and drove them out without visiting them. Behold, I am exacting justice from you according to your evil practices.
And I will receive the remnant of My people from all the land where I drove them out, and establish them in their pasture; they will increase and multiply.
And I will raise shepherds for them who will tend them, and they will no longer fear or be frightened, says the Lord.
A king is not saved through a great force, and a giant will not be saved by the abundance of his strength.
A horse is false for salvation, and by the abundance of its power it will not be saved.
Behold, the Lord’s eyes are upon those who fear Him, those who hope in His mercy,
to rescue their souls from death and nourish them in famine.
